claims.quote: "—spilt tea under the boards. Don't tell."
"Her name was Elsie L.," she said. "The photograph's date — October the twelfth, 1913."
I tilted the locket under the lamp. The shallow letters on the silver caught the light: E.L., rubbed and honest.
Beside it the sepia's smear resolved into the same date I had coaxed from the back of the photograph.

claims.value: dark, circular, tannin-brown with speckled edges and a tacky adhesive residue around the rim
claims.quote: Beneath the bundle of child's papers the subfloor showed a dark, circular mark: tannin-brown, the colour of over‑steeped tea, its edges specked with dust and a tacky, glue-like ring around the rim where something had been bound fast.

claims.value: braided ribbon matches diary description; diary line: 'I tied my ribbon to Doll's wrist so she'd remember me.'
claims.quote: The ribbon braided at its wrist matched the loop the diary's folded page suggested: a child had tied something on purpose. The diary itself mentioned fastening a ribbon to the doll so it would remember.

claims.value: sealed the cavity the same day; told people child was sent away
claims.quote: "I sealed that space myself the same day. I thought saying she was sent away would keep the questions away."

claims.value: can repeat child's phrases and make small, physical motions (doll movement; chalk E appearing; timed footfalls)
claims.quote: On the attic hatch, fresh white strokes formed the single, wobbly letter of a child's name: an E. ... The voice that followed did its small, circling thing: "Don't tell." ... When I set the doll on the joist it moved ... It slid sideways, nudged at the air and came to rest in my palm as if a small hand had placed it there. ... The measured footfalls that had occupied the house stopped as if someone had wound down a watch.

claims.value: presented torn diary page, locket, photograph date, and subfloor stain to force confession
claims.quote: I set the torn page, the locket and the close-up of the stain on the kitchen table and waited for the house to say its piece. ... I took her by the sleeve and we climbed the narrow ladder together.
